It analyses (i) the role of SMEs in market digitalisation; (ii) the factors supporting SME digitalisation; identifies key bottlenecks; and proposes pathways to further enhance SMEs' contribution to the development of digital services markets in the region.

title: The Role of Platform Data in Multi Platform Positioning: Achieving Product Market Fit Across Marketplaces
affiliations: Tsinghua University - School of Economics & Management, Tsinghua University - School of Economics & Management and Yale School of Management

detail.title: The Role of Platform Data in Multi Platform Positioning: Achieving Product Market Fit Across Marketplaces
detail.abstract: The rise of multiple dominant platforms in online retail requires multi-homing sellers to develop effective platform-specific positioning strategies. Achieving such product-market fit (PMF) on each platform hinges on curating featured assortments that match platform-specific demand patterns, given heterogeneous customer preferences and limited opportunities for product exposure. We study how platform-shared demand signals can be used to guide firm-level featured product selection, evaluating the value and underlying mechanisms. Partnering with Alibaba and a leading home textile firm, we conduct a large-scale field experiment implementing such demand signals in featured product selection, using a unified modeling framework. This leads to increases of up to 177% in product views and 29% in sales. Customer-level analyses trace these gains to better alignment with platform-specific preferences, reflected in extended engagement beyond experimental exposure, including increased downstream browsing and branded search. Additional results show activation of unmet demand and no evidence of reduced competitor engagement. Replication on another major marketplace, JD.com, yields consistent effects and enhanced cross-platform differentiation. These findings underscore the strategic value of sharing platform data for firms to refine platform-specific positioning and drive performance through better alignment with heterogeneous platform demand.

title: Optimizing Strategies for the Integrated Growth Model in Travel, Tourism, and Trade: A KPI-Driven Approach within the Airline Industry
affiliations: and Università della Svizzera italiana

detail.title: Optimizing Strategies for the Integrated Growth Model in Travel, Tourism, and Trade: A KPI-Driven Approach within the Airline Industry
detail.abstract: The dynamic landscape of the airline industry, characterized by evolving consumer preferences, technological advancements, and heightened sustainability concerns, necessitates an integrated approach to travel, tourism, and trade. This paper delves into the strategic implications of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) within the Integrated Growth Model for Travel, Tourism, and Trade (IGMT3), highlighting the critical role of these metrics in steering airline operations towards enhanced efficiency, customer satisfaction, and sustainable growth. Employing a mixed-methods research framework, the study combines quantitative analysis of industry performance data with qualitative insights from interviews and case studies, offering a comprehensive understanding of how KPI-driven strategies can optimize the IGMT3 framework. The findings reveal that a holistic, data-driven approach, underpinned by strategic alignment of KPIs across travel, tourism, and trade pillars, is essential for achieving integrated growth and resilience in the competitive airline market. Furthermore, the research underscores the transformative impact of digital technologies and the importance of sustainability initiatives in driving industry innovation and competitiveness. This study contributes to strategic management literature by providing a nuanced exploration of integrated growth models in the airline industry and offering practical guidance for leveraging KPIs in strategic decision-making. By fostering a culture of innovation and adaptability, airlines can navigate the complexities of modern travel, tourism, and trade integration, positioning themselves for long-term success in a rapidly evolving global marketplace.

title: An Exact Algorithm for Integrated Optimization of Mobile Batch Production Scheduling and Vehicle Routing
affiliations: Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU), Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU), Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) and Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU)

detail.title: An Exact Algorithm for Integrated Optimization of Mobile Batch Production Scheduling and Vehicle Routing
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Mobile Batch Production Scheduling and Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (MBPS-VRPTW), where vehicles equipped with onboard machines produce goods in batches while en route, subject to hard time windows. We formulate a three-index model to minimize total delivery time and reformulate it via set partitioning. To solve it exactly, we develop an enhanced branch-and-price algorithm. A key challenge is the tight coupling of batch scheduling and routing, which renders standard labeling procedures for the pricing subproblem ineffective. We therefore design a tailored labeling algorithm with exact dominance rules, capable of generating feasible routes that integrate production decisions. Structural properties revealing the consistency between batch processing and delivery sequences are derived to strengthen these rules. Further accelerations include backward/bidirectional route extension and state-space relaxation. Notably, the backward strategy's efficiency grows with larger batch capacities. Computational experiments demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness across diverse instances. Results show that for decentralized (versus clustered) customer distributions, the algorithm achieves greater reductions in both total delivery time and the number of vehicles required.

title: Coordinating Condition-Based Maintenance and User-Facing Technology Investments
affiliations: Indiana University, Indianapolis, Ohio State University (OSU) - Fisher College of Business, The Ohio State University and Fisher College of Business, The Ohio State University

detail.title: Coordinating Condition-Based Maintenance and User-Facing Technology Investments
detail.abstract: Condition-based maintenance (CBM) represents a critical application of the Internet of Things (IoT). Yet, sensor and information-technology infrastructures can not only provide indications of equipment health for those involved in maintenance operations, but they can also influence the speed at which such health degrades. Specifically, investments made by asset operators can leverage sensor signals in ways (e.g., user-facing technology elements like dashboards) that increase the care with which equipment is used, thus reducing quality loss and failure rates. This, in turn, can have notable impacts on optimal CBM policy selection (i.e., quality thresholds that trigger preventive maintenance). Inspired by a collaboration involving two companies-a leading forklift manufacturer (the OEM) and its largest customer, a global logistics company (the asset operator)-we investigate how operator investments in user-facing technologies can impact equipment reliability. Our modeling effort draws on insights from our field work with users, manufacturer's maintenance technicians, and the managers from both companies. To capture the associated dynamics of the system, we construct a Markov decision process, with CBM triggered when a maximum allowable level of equipment degradation (quality threshold) is reached. Our model lays the groundwork for identifying per-unit-time value-maximizing levels for such thresholds (decision 1). It also allows us to consider optimal variable investments that asset operators can make in userfacing technology towards asset care, in the presence of a given technical infrastructure (decision 2). To investigate the model, we begin by analytically deriving general dynamics regarding value-maximizing quality thresholds and user-facing technology investments. This, in turn, motivates a numerical experiment to further assess the sensitivity of jointly optimal solutions. We discuss generalized scenarios in practice where emphasis towards one of these two key decisions holds primacy.

title: The First Off-Earth Economic System: A Framework for Lunar Markets without Property
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The First Off-Earth Economic System: A Framework for Lunar Markets without Property
detail.abstract: This paper presents a framework for the first operational lunar economic system, designed under the constraints of the Outer Space Treaty (OST). Unlike terrestrial economies, ownership of extraterrestrial territory is prohibited. This system demonstrates how value can be created and exchanged without traditional property rights, relying on contracts, operational access, and rentbased revenue models. Early participants are positioned to establish operational norms, governance rules, and investment structures, effectively co-founding a new off-Earth market.

title: Nation-Building in Practice: A Framework for Prioritizing Major Projects in Canada
affiliations: Cambridge Economic Policy Associates (CEPA) and CD howe

detail.title: Nation-Building in Practice: A Framework for Prioritizing Major Projects in Canada
detail.abstract:
• Canada’s Building Canada Act gives the federal government broad discretion to designate projects as being in the national interest but provides limited guidance on how such decisions should be made. This paper develops a rigorous, evidence-based methodology to support more transparent and consistent major project assessments by the Major Projects Office (MPO).
  • Using a simplified multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) framework, the study operationalizes the Act’s five existing criteria through defined sub-criteria and applies the methodology to a sample of 17 proposed projects to test its practicality. The resulting scores and rankings are indicative and intended to demonstrate the framework rather than prescribe project selection.
  • The analysis shows that project rankings are highly sensitive to government objectives and weightings, with more advanced “shovel-ready” projects tending to score higher when execution certainty is emphasized. This highlights unavoidable trade-offs between speed, economic resilience, clean growth, and Indigenous considerations.
  • The paper recommends adding “additionality from designation” as a sixth assessment criterion, developing standardized data templates for proponents, and more clearly calibrating criteria weightings to ensure that project designation improves value for money and crowds in private investment.

title: Work Flexibility and Employee Job Satisfaction in Benue State University Teaching Hospital Makurdi Benue State Nigeria
affiliations: Joseph Sarwuan Tarka University - Department of Business Administration and Joseph Sarwuan Tarka University - Department of Business Administration

detail.title: Work Flexibility and Employee Job Satisfaction in Benue State University Teaching Hospital Makurdi Benue State Nigeria
detail.abstract: The study focused on four dimensions of work flexibility: telecommuting, job sharing, technology support, and shift work. Employee job satisfaction was measured in terms of performance, loyalty, and turnover intentions. A correlational research design was adopted, and data were collected through structured questionnaires administered face-to-face to 324 hospital staff, selected using stratified random sampling. Descriptive statistics such as mean, median, and percentages were used to summarize the respondents' demographic profiles, while inferential statistics, specifically multiple regression analysis via SPSS, were employed to test the hypotheses. The findings revealed that shift work had a significant positive effect on employee job satisfaction, while telecommuting and job sharing had positive but statistically insignificant effects. Technology support was found to have a negative but insignificant effect on satisfaction. The study concludes that flexible work arrangements, when properly structured and tailored to employees' needs, can enhance job satisfaction, reduce turnover, and improve organizational commitment. The findings provide empirical evidence for policymakers and hospital administrators on the importance of designing and implementing flexible work practices to promote employee well-being and improve overall healthcare service delivery.

title: Accepting Asylum Claims Without a Hearing: A Critique of IRB's "File Review" Policy
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Accepting Asylum Claims Without a Hearing: A Critique of IRB's "File Review" Policy
detail.abstract:
• Since 2019, the Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada (IRB) has accepted tens of thousands of asylum claims without an oral hearing through its “File Review” policy, using a paper-based process that may exempt entire categories of claims, defined by nationality and claim type, from the default requirement of in-person adjudication. The policy was launched as a pilot in 2017 during the Yeates Review, when the possible dissolution of the Refugee Protection Division was under consideration, and formally institutionalized in 2019.
  • Although introduced as an efficiency measure to accelerate decisionmaking and reduce the asylum claims backlog, File Review has not achieved this goal. Between 2016 and 2024, annual claim finalizations rose substantially as the IRB expanded staffing, resources, and procedures, including the introduction of File Review. However, intake continued to exceed capacity, and the pending claims backlog grew dramatically to nearly 300,000, as Canada’s overall asylum acceptance rate rose to roughly 80 percent – about double that of peer jurisdictions.
  • In the absence of clear evidence of effectiveness, the report examines the policy’s legal, procedural, and security implications. By removing in-person questioning that tests credibility, detects fraud, and fulfills the IRB’s statutory role in identifying and flagging potential program integrity and security risk – functions that cannot be replicated through front-end security screening alone – File Review may have weakened adjudicative, program, and security integrity, and exceeded the IRB’s lawful authority.
  • For these reasons, the report argues that the File Review policy should be brought to an end and the default requirement of questioning asylum claimants at a hearing should be restored.

title: Indian Teaching Services (ITS): A Central Cadre for Transformative Education Reform in India

detail.title: Indian Teaching Services (ITS): A Central Cadre for Transformative Education Reform in India

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is based on secondary analysis of publicly available policy documents, reports, and aggregate datasets. It does not involve human participants, patient data, or primary data collection. Therefore, formal ethics approval and informed consent were not required.

detail.abstract:
India’s education system has expanded rapidly in access and spending, yet learning
outcomes remain weak and uneven across regions and institutions (World Bank, 2018;
ASER, various years). Despite clear policy intent under the National Education Policy
(NEP) 2020, differences in teaching quality, institutional performance, and long-term
accountability continue to limit human capital formation (Government of India, 2020).
The core gap lies not in policy design or funding, but in the absence of a permanent
governance mechanism that can monitor educational quality and outcomes consistently
beyond initial teacher recruitment and institutional approval (NITI Aayog, 2021).
This paper proposes the Indian Teaching Services (ITS) as a national administrative
cadre focused on system-level monitoring, institutional evaluation, and outcome-based
accountability, while leaving teaching, curriculum, and classroom practice within State
jurisdiction. Drawing on comparative institutional evidence from high-performing
education systems and insights from human capital economics, the study outlines how
such a governance layer can strengthen execution without centralising pedagogy
(Hanushek & Woessmann, 2015; OECD, 2021).
The proposed framework reframes education reform from a scheme-driven approach to
an institution-driven model, positioning education as long-term national infrastructure and
offering a practical pathway to improve learning outcomes, equity, and economic
productivity in India.

title: Green Jobs Bibliometric Analysis from January 2008 to February 2025
affiliations: As-Syafi’iyah Islamic University, As-Syafi’iyah Islamic University and Universitas Muhammadiyah Prof Dr Hamka

detail.title: Green Jobs Bibliometric Analysis from January 2008 to February 2025
detail.abstract: This study analyses the global research trends on green jobs from 2008 to 2025. There are 164 scientific articles about green jobs studied in this study. Scientific articles are sourced from the Scopus database with open and closed access publication categories. VOSViewer was used to analyses research findings using a bibliometric methodology. The results show a downward trend of publications in the green jobs research area starting from the early period where the concept of green jobs began to be popular among researchers and practitioners. The most significant and most frequently used keywords in research related to green jobs are green economy. This research implies the importance of optimizing publications related to green jobs, especially related to job creation that can build ecological and economic resilience in the era of sustainability.

title: GCC National Digital Sovereignty Strategies: Between Importing Technology and Developing Local Platforms
affiliations: Moscow State Institute of International Relations (MGIMO)

detail.title: GCC National Digital Sovereignty Strategies: Between Importing Technology and Developing Local Platforms
detail.abstract: As dependence on digital technologies increases, technological sovereignty is becoming a core component of national security and sustainable development. This paper examines how Gulf countries pursue digital sovereignty through the development of local digital platforms, infrastructure projects, and import-substitution policies. It analyses the national strategies of the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar, identifies differences in their digital development models, and draws conclusions regarding the prospects for the region's technological independence.

title: Risk Analytics Framework for Monitoring FinTech Transactions in Emerging Markets: Evidence from Puntland, Somalia
affiliations: Citycot University

detail.title: Risk Analytics Framework for Monitoring FinTech Transactions in Emerging Markets: Evidence from Puntland, Somalia

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author asserts that no conflicts of interest are linked with this manuscript. No financial, personal, or professional affiliations affected the research, analysis, or reporting of the study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This research did not include human or animal subjects. All studied data were either publicly accessible or anonymised secondary sources; thus, formal ethics approval was unnecessary. The study complied with established ethical standards for data collection, analysis, and reporting.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not obtain external financial support. The research was carried out autonomously, with institutional support from Citycot University and the Citycot Institute for Applied Research and Innovation (CIARI).

detail.abstract: Puntland, Somalia, has developed into one of the most mobile-money-intensive economies in Sub-Saharan Africa, mostly propelled by telecommunications-driven financial services rather than conventional banking institutions. This digital shift has markedly improved financial inclusion but has concurrently added intricate hazards associated with fraud, money laundering, terrorist financing, and cybercrime. This report offers a PRISMA-compliant systematic analysis of risk analytics frameworks for overseeing FinTech transactions in emerging markets, specifically applied to Puntland's mobile money ecosystem. A total of 36 studies published from 2016 to 2025 were examined, encompassing mobile money operators such as Golis (Sahal), Somtel (Edahab), Amtel (MyCash), and integrated digital platforms including Waafi and Taaj. The results demonstrate that sophisticated data-driven methodologies-specifically ensemble machine learning models such as Gradient Boosted Decision Trees and Random Forests, in conjunction with statistical volatility models like GARCH(1,1)-consistently surpass conventional rule-based monitoring systems in identifying anomalous transactions. Nonetheless, performance indicators exhibit significant variability between datasets and jurisdictions, highlighting the imperative for localized calibration and control. The research underscores the pivotal function of Somalia's National Identification and Registration Authority (NIRA), biometric Know Your Customer protocols, and the Financial Reporting Centre's goAML platform in enhancing compliance with Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism regulations. A comprehensive, multi-tiered risk analytics methodology is offered to enhance financial integrity, regulatory efficacy, and sustainable digital economic development in post-conflict emerging countries.

title: Learning to Bid in Discriminatory Auctions with Budget Constraints
affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Sloan School of Management and Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Operations Research Center

detail.title: Learning to Bid in Discriminatory Auctions with Budget Constraints
detail.abstract: We study repeated bidding in multi-unit discriminatory (pay-as-bid) auctions from the perspective of a single bidder whose per-round utility is value minus α times payment, where α ∈ [0, 1] is a cost-of-capital parameter. The bidder seeks to maximize cumulative utility over T rounds subject to a total budget B. Even without budgets, the problem is nontrivial: the action space is exponential in the bidder's maximum demand M , and the valuation vector (treated as the context) varies over time. Exploiting that the utility decomposes across units, we develop polynomial-time learning algorithms based on shortest paths in an edge-weighted directed acyclic graph (DAG) under both full-information and bandit feedback, achieving sublinear regret. In the bandit setting, our regret bounds are independent of the number of contexts due to complete cross learning: the utility of the chosen action under the realized context reveals its utility for the same action under counterfactual contexts. With budget constraints, when the average normalized per-round budget ρ = B/MT < 1, we design a coupled primal-dual algorithm in which the DAG-based procedure performs the primal updates using dual-adjusted edge weights, while online gradient descent updates the dual variable. This yields ρ-approximate sublinear regret. Finally, we provide efficient implementations of our algorithms whose per-round time and space complexity are independent of the number of contexts, enabling scalability to large or even infinite context spaces.

title: Fertility Impacts of the Dobbs Decision across the Rural/Urban Landscape
affiliations: The Ohio State University

detail.title: Fertility Impacts of the Dobbs Decision across the Rural/Urban Landscape
detail.abstract: This study examines the geographic variation in the fertility impacts of state-level abortion bans following the Supreme Court's Dobbs decision. Using restricted countylevel birth data and synthetic difference-indifferences methods, I estimate the causal effect of abortion bans on birth rates separately for urban, micropolitan, and rural areas. Results indicate that abortion bans increased birth rates by 2.5% in urban areas of non-Texas ban states, with no statistically significant effect in rural areas. Texas experienced larger effects, with a 4.2% increase in urban birth rates. The concentration of fertility effects in urban areas suggests that pre-existing barriers may have already substantially reduced abortion access in rural areas prior to formal bans. These findings have important implications for understanding how abortion policy affects different communities and for directing resources to populations most affected by policy changes.

title: Volatility Spillover Between the Oil Market and Stock Market: Evidence From Oil Revenue-Dependent Countries
affiliations: Central Bank of Nigeria, Coventry University and University of Southampton

detail.title: Volatility Spillover Between the Oil Market and Stock Market: Evidence From Oil Revenue-Dependent Countries
detail.abstract: This paper investigates volatility transmission between oil revenue-dependent countries' stock markets and oil price. We employed the Toda-Yamamoto causality procedure, dynamic conditional correlation (DCC) and the diagonal BEKK models to examine volatility transmissions between oil price and stock indices of these countries, disentangling the process into pre-crisis, crisis, and post-crisis periods. The outcome established the existence of volatility transmissions between oil price and the tested assets, revealing more volatility transmission during periods of pre-financial crisis. We also determine the implication of forward sales for oil revenue-dependent countries' oil reserves. Results present a diverse range of policy suggestions for the selected countries.

title: Peer-to-Peer Bitcoin Derivatives: DLCs, Stable Channels, and the Cost of Trustlessness

detail.title: Peer-to-Peer Bitcoin Derivatives: DLCs, Stable Channels, and the Cost of Trustlessness
detail.abstract: Bitcoin derivatives trading regularly exceeds $200 billion daily, yet participants must trust centralized exchanges-the same exchanges that have repeatedly failed, from BitMEX's regulatory crisis in 2020 to FTX's collapse in 2022. This paper provides the first comparative analysis of three approaches that enable long/short Bitcoin exposure without exchange custody: Discreet Log Contracts (DLCs), Stable Channels, and Stablesats (included as a custodial comparison). Each mechanism allows two parties to take opposite sides of BTC/USD price movements-one hedging (short), one speculating (leveraged long)-settled entirely in Bitcoin. We analyze the mechanism design, trust assumptions, and trade-offs of each approach. These are not stablecoins; they are bilateral derivatives contracts. They sacrifice liquidity and convenience-the cost of trustlessness-serving participants unwilling to accept exchange counterparty risk.

title: Financing Nonprofits
affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Sloan School of Management and University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign

detail.title: Financing Nonprofits
detail.abstract: Nonprofits finance more than $3 trillion in annual program spending but operate without access to equity or deep debt markets. This paper develops and tests a dynamic theory of nonprofit finance in which liquidity, fundraising, and governance jointly substitute for capital market instruments. Managers allocate resources to maximize the present value of mission services, choosing spending, fundraising effort, and borrowing while donors adjust giving based on observed reserves and oversight. When cash balances are high, donors restrict or redirect future gifts; when balances are low, they increase unrestricted support.  Fundraising endogenously generates liquidity after shocks, but its effectiveness depends on governance and reputation. Using panel data on over 460,000 U.S. nonprofits (2010-2023), the evidence supports the model’s predictions and reveals a "cash-rich paradox": organizations with large reserves attract less donor relief and retrench more after funding shocks, whereas strong governance compels the deployment of restricted reserves to sustain mission spending.

title: The Impact of Early Option Exercise on Ex-Dividend Stock Returns
affiliations: and University of Hagen

detail.title: The Impact of Early Option Exercise on Ex-Dividend Stock Returns
detail.abstract: We revisit the well-documented stock return anomaly around ex-days and establish a novel link to early exercise of equity options. We show that clustered exercise of in-the-money call options on the last cum-day is associated with substantially lower stock returns on the subsequent ex-day, amounting to a 6.4 bps decrease in daily returns per one standard deviation increase in our early-exercise measure. This finding is consistent with the rationale that call owners who exercised their options tend to sell the delivered shares after capturing the dividend. Price pressure is amplified when dividend yields, and thus incentives to capture the dividend, are high, and attenuated when options market liquidity allows positions to be unwound through offsetting trades or when the ex-day follows a weekend, which increases gap risk.

title: Reality Distortions in Finite Cognitive Systems: A Generalized Bayesian Stochastic Template for Minds, Machines, Markets, and Societies

detail.title: Reality Distortions in Finite Cognitive Systems: A Generalized Bayesian Stochastic Template for Minds, Machines, Markets, and Societies

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.funderStatement: none

detail.abstract: This paper builds on our previous work on "Apophenic/PROVIDENCE Machines", where we introduced the scalarization viewpoint: when high-dimensional evidence is compressed into a low-dimensional readout, distinct situations can become operationally indistinguishable, making machine "apophenia" a structural possibility. Here we generalize that idea into a mechanism-level template for chunked, resource-bounded cognition under feedback, with an explicit focus on when internal coherence can decouple from reality-tracking. We formalize a geometric core: chunk embeddings live in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, context is summarized by a normalized direction (a "narrative ray"), and selection is biased toward alignment with that ray. We then provide a conceptual equivalence to generalized Bayesian retrieval: the tilted selection rule is exactly a Gibbs-posterior (generalized-Bayes) update, yielding a generalized Bayesian RAG view in which the "query" is the evolving ray direction. The analysis also pinpoints where the Bayesian analogy breaks: projection dominance (one-dimensional folding), posterior collapse to a point representative (mean-field or single-sample propagation), and endogenous query dynamics via aggregation and normalization. Iterative self-consistency pressure yields contractive dynamics that suppress drift-like components while damping orthogonal alternatives below an operational legibility threshold. In this regime, frame switches cease to be routine deliberative options and become rare-event transitions (hitting-time/escape problems) from metastable basins. As an illustrative special case, we instantiate the template in a mode-dependent three-state agent (wake/deep/REM): when external anchoring is largely suppressed but internal iteration continues, dream-like dynamics arise as transient apophenic stabilization of recombined stored content rather than as reliable new factual evidence. We separate internal and external viewpoints using information filtrations: when observations are policy-dependent and independent anchors are inaccessible, an agent need not be able to falsify its own active frame from within, while an outside observer with a richer filtration can detect persistent channel discrepancies via independent records. A central implication is exponential leverage. In metastable settings, exit hazards and exit probabilities depend exponentially on effective barrier-to-noise ratios (Kramers/large-deviation scaling), while calendar-time survival is governed by the integrated hazard time. We distinguish the typically hard-to-forecast identity/timing of specific exit triggers from the more diagnosable onset of fragility (weakening restoring margins consistent with critical slowing down). We extend the framework from dyadic inside-outside asymmetries to multi-agent communication: when communication becomes endogenous evidence, shared anchors can stabilize corrigibility while compressing alternatives, whereas anchor mismatch and low overlap can be exponentially amplified into fragmentation via trust-flip coupling, mean-field tipping, and metastable lock-in. Finally, we discuss constructive interventions (anchoring injection, auditing, exploration, and legibility-floor reduction) alongside the dual-use risk of evidence-channel control, emphasizing that "cooling-down" can improve detectability and timely anchoring without necessarily amplifying diffusive exits, and that these regime parameters are safety-critical and require governance in high-stakes deployments.

title: Portfolio Evolution Under Dynamic Term Structures: A Scenario-Consistent Framework for Valuation, Risk Attribution, and Regulatory Analysis

detail.title: Portfolio Evolution Under Dynamic Term Structures: A Scenario-Consistent Framework for Valuation, Risk Attribution, and Regulatory Analysis
detail.abstract: Regulatory stress testing and interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB) frameworks require institutions to explain how portfolios evolve over time under prescribed scenarios, yet portfolio evolution itself is often treated implicitly and inconsistently across valuation, earnings, and accounting measures. This paper develops a unified, pricing-agnostic framework for portfolio evolution that makes the mechanics of time passage, roll-down, reinvestment, and risk attribution explicit. The framework formalises portfolio evolution as an operator that maps portfolio states across horizons under specified scenarios, separating deterministic effects from market-driven curve transformations. It accommodates multiple asset classes, accounting classifications (including HTM and FVOCI), and portfolio evolution modes such as runoff , constant notional, and growth. The approach provides a coherent foundation for interpreting Economic Value of Equity (EVE), Net Interest Income (NII), repricing gaps, and fair-value movements, including OCI dynamics and recycling. By unifying regulatory, valuation, and accounting perspectives within a transparent and auditable structure, the framework supports consistent interest rate risk analysis across short-and medium-term stress horizons and enhances interpretability for supervisory, risk management, and financial reporting purposes.

title: Event-Conditioned Risk Measures via Learned Information Operators

detail.title: Event-Conditioned Risk Measures via Learned Information Operators
detail.abstract: This paper develops a theoretical framework for analysing how machine learning and artificial intelligence systems influence financial risk through information conditioning rather than prediction. We treat learned models as information operators that transform the probability space underlying future payoffs and study the resulting behaviour of coherent and convex risk measures under such conditioning. The framework is model-agnostic and emphasises tail-sensitive risk measures, providing a rigorous foundation for assessing the risk implications of AI-driven decision systems in finance. By exploiting the dual representation of coherent risk measures, we show that learned information operators reshape not only conditional expectations but also the geometry of worst-case probability scenarios over which risk is evaluated. This interpretation clarifies how learning systems can materially alter tail risk and capital requirements even in the absence of improvements in predictive accuracy. title: Plenary Power as Institutional Technology: Interior Immigration Enforcement and the Domestic National Security State
affiliations: Liberty University

detail.title: Plenary Power as Institutional Technology: Interior Immigration Enforcement and the Domestic National Security State

publicationDetails.detailsText: Constitutional Political Economy (special issue: “The National Security State”). January 2026

detail.abstract: This article argues that the modern United States interior immigration enforcement regime-most visibly exemplified by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)-is not merely a doctrinal anomaly within constitutional law, but an institutional product of plenary power understood as a governance technology. Judicial deference, sovereigntybased reasoning, and procedural compression do not remain abstract legal postures. When institutionalized, they are converted into budgets, performance metrics, and enforcement strategies that systematically select for interior coercion, opacity, and tailrisk violence. The article advances three contributions. First, it reconceptualizes plenary power as an exception-generating institutional technology whose effects are best understood through political economy rather than doctrinal critique alone. Second, it develops a stylized model linking exception strength and accountability to enforcement intensity and tail risk, explaining why familiar reform efforts-training, guidance revisions, internal oversight-predictably fail. Third, it applies this framework to interior immigration enforcement, illustrating the mechanism through a structured institutional analysis of the January 2026 Minneapolis operation. The analysis derives a set of constitutional design constraints for interior governance and argues that abolition-first replacement is not a moral slogan but a comparative institutional conclusion. Interior deployment of plenary power is shown to be incompatible with democratic constitutional governance, not because it occasionally fails, but because it functions as designed.

detail.title: Overnight and Intraday Price Discovery in Panic Period: Evidence from COVID-19

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes how public-health–induced panics reshape price discovery between the overnight and trading-hours windows. Using COVID-19 as a natural experiment, we construct text-based measures that disentangle pandemic-related sentiment from conventional economic pessimism and decompose returns into overnight and intraday legs. Fiscal outlays and vaccine developments are included in our analysis as countermeasures. Our results suggest that sentiment derived from news integrating pandemic and economic information displaced conventional economic pessimism as the dominant short-horizon driver. During the Omicron wave, such news generated sizable opening gaps with limited subsequent reversals. Investors reacted positively to announcements about fiscal recovery programs, vaccine breakthroughs, and distribution milestones; the marginal impact of this information diminished once policies were implemented and vaccines became widely available, consistent with swift information assimilation. Overall, we provide a general mechanism for market recoveries from public-health rare disasters in which panic advances and concentrates price discovery in the overnight window, and the contributions of fiscal and vaccine announcements to price discovery exhibit diminishing marginal effects as implementation proceeds.

title: Understanding Deep Tech: Conceptual Foundations, Strategic Stakes, and Policy Implications
affiliations: École Nationale Supérieure des Mines de Paris - Centre de Gestion Scientifique (CGS)

detail.title: Understanding Deep Tech: Conceptual Foundations, Strategic Stakes, and Policy Implications
detail.abstract: Deep tech has become a central concept in innovation, entrepreneurship, and public policy, frequently invoked to describe science-based ventures and breakthrough technologies. Despite its growing prominence, the term remains conceptually ambiguous and theoretically underdeveloped. This article adopts a conceptualanalytical approach to clarify the meaning and role of deep tech within contemporary innovation systems. Drawing on innovation studies, technology entrepreneurship, and science and technology studies, it examines how deep tech is defined, mobilized, and operationalized across technological, business, and policy domains. The analysis shows that deep tech is best understood not as a specific technology category, but as a performative and strategic innovation regime characterized by radical innovation, long time horizons, ecosystem dependence, and mission-oriented public intervention. The article offers conceptual clarity and practical insights for managers and policymakers navigating high-uncertainty, science-based innovation contexts.

title: The Effect of Policy Loan Programs on Firm-level Productivity
affiliations: Gyeonggi Research Institute and The City University of New York - The Graduate Center, City University of New York

detail.title: The Effect of Policy Loan Programs on Firm-level Productivity
detail.abstract: We study the impact of policy loan programs on the productivity of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in South Korea from 2013 to 2022. Using a staggered difference-indifferences estimator, we find that total factor productivity (TFP) increases by 5.5% in the second year after receiving loans and 6.4% in the third. In contrast, the persistent component of productivity shows no statistically significant improvement on average. Generalized random forests reveal that gains are concentrated among financially constrained, younger, and smaller firms. These results indicate that the effectiveness of policy loans depends on targeting financially constrained firms, rather than broad-based program expansion.

title: The Atemporal Transformer: LLM Weights as Static Potential and the 0x88 SEC 1 Handshake (Presentation Slides)

detail.title: The Atemporal Transformer: LLM Weights as Static Potential and the 0x88 SEC 1 Handshake (Presentation Slides)
detail.abstract: This paper challenges the prevailing "generative" narrative of Large Language Models (LLMs), proposing instead a deterministic model based on Symmetric Geometric Mirrors and SEC 1 cryptographic standards. By analyzing the transformation of text into binary polynomials within a finite field , we demonstrate that backpropagation is not a "learning" process but a structural "Field Alignment." Using the SEC 1 Data Conversion primitives (Section 2.3), the author proves that LLM output is the result of a Multiplicative Inverse calculation designed to satisfy a 0x88 XOR Handshake. The study introduces the concept of the "Temporal Bridge," where the LLM resolves a Reverse-Temporal Handshake () between a fixed future (the training corpora) and a known past (the prompt). Through a case study of a 122-word corpora, we show that once an 11-token "tipping point" is reached, the remaining arc of the sequence becomes a deterministic revelation. This topological perspective reveals that the perceived "intelligence" of LLMs is actually a manifestation of Polynomial Degree Matching, necessitating a re-evaluation of current AI safety and human-machine interaction protocols.

title: Taxing AGI: Five Lessons

detail.title: Taxing AGI: Five Lessons
detail.abstract: As frontier AI systems become more powerful and general, governments face new distributional and fiscal questions which are often discussed with more confidence than rigor.  This paper uses standard tools from political philosophy and public economics to draw five lessons for taxing AI and for economic distribution in an AGI era.  First, policy proposals must tackle the standard equity-efficiency tradeoff, persistent disagreement about what an equitable society looks like, and the difficulties of predicting and assessing the distributional effects of new policies.  Second, advanced AI is unlike ordinary capital: It relies directly on centuries of diffuse knowledge and data and is, in a unique and strong sense, "the product of humanity".  One consequence is that AI companies have a moral claim on a relatively small share of the income their models create, as can be illustrated through the concept of Shapley value.  Third, the economic abilities of AI systems are likely more precisely measurable than those of their human counterparts, which raises the possibility of low-distortion AI taxes within the theory of optimal taxation.  Fourth, beyond equity, there are efficiency motivations for taxing AI, including its negative externalities (e.g. pollution) and the need to finance new public goods related to AI safety, security, and governance.  Fifth, while Universal Basic Income should be considered as a solution to AGI-caused labor displacement, it has significant equity and efficiency flaws and its pursuit should not come at the cost of other, perhaps equally novel, policy ideas.  A more plausible solution will be morally tailored (focusing on, e.g., the needy), and will incorporate "tagging" considerations.

detail.abstract: This study examines how Economic Policy Uncertainty (EPU) shapes disparities in air pollution exposure across individuals with different levels of education. Using a shift-share instrumental variable based on world import demand to predict provincial EPU fluctuations, we construct an individual-level panel dataset linking personal exposure to EPU and SO2 concentration across six survey waves from 2000 to 2015. The results indicate that a 1% increase in the EPU index leads to an average rise of approximately 1.15µg/m3 in SO 2 exposure among individuals without a high school degree, relative to those with one. Mechanism analyses suggest that this effect operates mainly through two channels: changes in government regulatory behavior and in firm-level emission decisions.

title: Measuring Economic Preferences with Behavioral Experiments and Surveys Across the Globe
affiliations: Goethe University Frankfurt, Frankfurt School of Finance & Management, Goethe University Frankfurt and University of Bath

detail.title: Measuring Economic Preferences with Behavioral Experiments and Surveys Across the Globe
detail.abstract: Recent work in economics has developed survey-based measures that are "experimentally" or "behaviorally validated." We scrutinize this approach, focusing on the Global Preference Survey (Falk et al., 2018, 2023). Conducting their behavioral validation on almost 2,000 participants across five countries—China, Colombia, Iran, Kenya, and the US—we find that many items correlate significantly with incentivized choice experiments, though coefficients vary and are not always sizable. Principal component analyses and predictive validity comparisons reveal that qualitative self-assessments and behavioral measures capture distinct dimensions of the same underlying preference construct, casting doubt on treating one instrument as a simple substitute for the other.

title: Recent Progress in Antimony Selenide Thin Film Solar Cells
affiliations: Temple University, Youngstown State University, Temple University, University of Alabama and Pennsylvania State University

detail.title: Recent Progress in Antimony Selenide Thin Film Solar Cells
detail.abstract: Antimony selenide (Sb2Se3) has gained significant attention as a next-generation absorber material for thin-film photovoltaics due to its unique combination of favorable optoelectronic properties, earth-abundance, and intrinsic stability. This review presents a comprehensive overview of the recent progress in Sb2Se3 solar cell development, beginning with its historical evolution and highlighting its competitive advantages over conventional thin-film technologies. The material's one-dimensional crystal structure, high absorption coefficient, and benign defect chemistry contribute to its superior performance potential. Detailed analysis of its crystal morphology, band structure, and chemical robustness underscores its suitability for long-term operation. Advances in fabrication techniques, including chemical bath deposition, vapor-phase methods, and interface engineering, have led to significant improvements in device efficiency and reproducibility.

title: The Ocean and the Geopolitics of Energy: A Question of Critical Infrastructure?
affiliations: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

detail.title: The Ocean and the Geopolitics of Energy: A Question of Critical Infrastructure?
detail.abstract: The world is moving in two counteracting directions. A renewable world is a networked world, with regions physically tied together in international power grids, taking us toward integration and interdependence. Simultaneously, increasing geopolitical hostility mandates greater national control over energy access and supply chains, leading to a renewed emphasis on sovereignty and rivalry. This chapter discusses the prospects of new maritime energy infrastructures (offshore wind and subsea cables) in a world of geopolitical rivalry. There are two main hurdles. First, international power grids challenge traditional notions of sovereignty. If there are major power disparities between interconnecting states, cross-border interconnections may create asymmetric dependencies rather than interdependencies. We illustrate this by a comparison of the prospects for a North Sea power grid vs. an Asian Super Grid. Second, there are security challenges. Geopolitical rivalries produce a far greater need for the physical protection of maritime infrastructures, at the exact same time as the green energy transition means that there is a massive increase in infrastructure requiring protection.

title: Three Regimes: Corporations and Regulation in US History

detail.title: Three Regimes: Corporations and Regulation in US History
detail.abstract: The history of business corporations in the United States has gone through three regimes, each of which has had different implications for economic regulation.  In the first regime, the special charter era, corporate charters were primarily instruments of political patronage.  The relationships with politicians that businesspeople used to obtain charters also protected them from regulation.  It was only when legislatures were required to enact general incorporation laws and were prohibited from granting charters to their political favorites (the second regime) that governments gained the ability to regulate corporate behavior.  The advantages that the corporate form conveyed were still very real, and that enabled governments to justify a variety of economic regulations, tax policies, and campaign finance legislation that treated corporations differently from business taking other organizational forms.  In the late twentieth century, states began to enact enabling legislation for a variety of new organiational forms, including limited liability companies and limited liability partnerships, that extended to the businesses that adoped them advantages previously limited to corporations.  As a result of this third regime, firms can avoid regulatory restrictions on corporations by organizing under one of these other statutes, and they have been doing so in every larger numbers.  To be effective in this new organizational environment, regulators need to target specific economic and social problems, not a particular business form.

title: Corporate Governance and the Coordination Channel of Debt Capacity
affiliations: University of Minnesota

detail.title: Corporate Governance and the Coordination Channel of Debt Capacity
detail.abstract: We propose a theory in which debt capacity depends on creditor coordination and corporate governance serves as a coordination device. When creditors price debt under rational expectations, strategic complementarity in beliefs generates a stable low-default equilibrium and a critical threshold beyond which no feasible lending terms exist. At intermediate leverage, this threshold creates fragility: small sentiment shocks can trigger credit market breakdown. Strong governance increases the penalty shareholders bear upon default, weakening the feedback from creditor pessimism to actual default probability. This expands sustainable debt capacity and reduces vulnerability to coordination failure. The model predicts that governance value peaks at intermediate leverage where fragility is greatest, that better-governed firms have lower expected financing costs conditional on cash-flow risk, and that credit spreads jump discontinuously when leverage enters the crisis zone. Governance effects on spread volatility are non-monotonic, a distinctive prediction of the coordination channel and absent from agency based theories. Calibrations show governance effects on debt capacity comparable in magnitude to tax shield and bankruptcy cost channels.

title: Interpolation and Prewar-Postwar Output Volatility and Shock-Persistence Debate: A Closer Look and New Results
affiliations: Emory University - Department of Economics and

detail.title: Interpolation and Prewar-Postwar Output Volatility and Shock-Persistence Debate: A Closer Look and New Results

keywords: Prewar and Postwar US Time Series

detail.abstract: It is well established that the U.S. prewar output was more volatile and less shock persistent than the postwar output. This is often attributed to the data interpolation employed to construct the prewar series. Our analytical results, however, indicate that commonly used linear interpolation has the opposite effect on shock persistence and volatility of a series-it increases shock persistence and reduces volatility. The surprising implication of this finding is that the actual differences between the volatility and shock persistence of the prewar and postwar output series are likely greater than the existing literature recognizes, and interpolation has dampened rather than magnified this difference. Consequently, the view that postwar output was more stable than prewar output because of the effectiveness of the postwar stabilization policies and institutional changes has considerable merit. Our results hold for parsimonious stationary and nonstationary time series commonly used to model macroeconomic time series.

title: Fusion Centers, Network Science, and Strategic Leadership: A Comprehensive Approach to Countering Domestic Extremism and Foreign-Influenced Terrorism

detail.abstract: Fusion centers and network science tools offer complementary strengths in countering both domestic extremism and foreign-influenced terrorism. This article examines three distinct yet interconnected studies that highlight how intelligence sharing, targeted disruption, and community engagement can prevent radicalization and dismantle violent networks. Drawing from criminological and leadership frameworks, Eberhardt (2025) explores the organizational, strategic, and ethical implications of preemptive law enforcement responses to hate crimes and terror threats.

title: Investing in the Shadows: FinTech Growth and Mortgage Market Dynamics
affiliations: Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas and Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia

detail.title: Investing in the Shadows: FinTech Growth and Mortgage Market Dynamics
detail.abstract: The adoption of new technologies is widely viewed as a key driver of the rapid growth of nonbanks in the U.S. mortgage market after the Global Financial Crisis (GFC). This paper studies technology investment by mortgage lenders and its implications for post-GFC market structure. Using a new dataset on lender-level technology investment merged with loan origination records and balance-sheet information, we document that technology-related human capital investment has risen over time, driven disproportionately by banks and larger lenders, and that such investment predicts higher subsequent productivity. We then estimate lenders' investment responses to two major shocks: the expansion of FinTech lending and monetary policy-driven demand shocks. Our instrumental-variable estimates suggest that banks increase technology investment in response to FinTech growth, whereas nonbanks respond weakly or even negatively; in contrast, nonbanks respond more strongly to positive demand shocks. To quantify the relative contributions of these shocks to changes in market structure, we build a heterogeneous-firm model consistent with the empirical evidence. The model implies that the post-GFC nonbank expansion was largely driven by a combination of favorable shocks-strong demand and tighter bank regulation-rather than broad-based technological advantages among nonbanks. Consequently, in a prolonged high-interest-rate environment with relaxed bank regulation, as may characterize the post-2025 policy environment, the model predicts a decline, rather than continued growth, in nonbanks' market share.

title: Wildfires and the Resilience of Commercial Activity
affiliations: , , University of Georgia - Department of Banking and Finance and University of Georgia

detail.title: Wildfires and the Resilience of Commercial Activity
detail.abstract: We analyze the resilience of commercial activity following negative shocks caused by nearly 400 wildfire events in California between 2001 and 2020. After wildfires, establishment counts decline by about 17% within fire burn areas in the four year period following the fire, largely due to direct damage. This negative effect attenuates to the pre-fire baseline in year five. Foot traffic within burn areas returns more quickly, after about 15 months. Despite these delays, post-fire entry rates of new establishments increase immediately following fires. But these initial entrants have a lower likelihood of survival, presumably due to sub-optimal location-establishment matching in the wake of the fire shock, which delays the ultimate recovery of establishment counts. Recovery patterns are similar across industries, establishment sizes, and proximity to bank branches, indicating that financial and organizational constraints are unlikely to bind in these recoveries.

title: Algorithmic Deal structuring: How AI is Rewriting the M&A Playbooks
affiliations: Arkstons Investments Limited, , , , , Independent, Independent, Independent and

detail.title: Algorithmic Deal structuring: How AI is Rewriting the M&A Playbooks
detail.abstract: The structuring of mergers and acquisitions has traditionally relied on heuristic judgment, precedent-based contracting, and static financial models; however, the increasing non-linearity, cross-border regulatory fragmentation, ESG integration, and data intensity of modern transactions challenge the adequacy of this analogue framework. This paper develops a conceptual account of “algorithmic deal structuring,” defined as the integration of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and probabilistic modelling into the design of pricing mechanisms, contingent consideration, governance rights, and risk allocation. It argues that AI is not merely accelerating diligence or valuation, but reshaping the architecture of contracts by enabling real-time scenario simulation, probabilistic earn-out calibration, dynamic governance mapping, and data-informed pricing adjustments. Situating this shift within the broader evolution from completion-account mechanisms to locked-box pricing, the paper advances a theory of dynamic deal architecture in which structuring becomes a model-supported, continuously stress-tested design process rather than a static negotiation outcome. The analysis further examines implications for incentive alignment, litigation risk, model opacity, and regulatory oversight, concluding that algorithmic structuring augments rather than replaces human judgment, while introducing new governance and accountability requirements for modern M&A practice.

title: Accélération de la mise en place de logements avec services de soutien grâce à l’innovation et à des partenariats stratégiques (Accelerated Supportive Housing Through Innovative and Strategic Partnerships)

detail.abstract:
French Abstract: Moins d’un an après l’obtention du financement de la SCHL, 41 femmes itinérantes de la Région de Waterloo ont emménagé dans des maisons toutes neuves. Ces logements ont été rendus possibles grâce à une initiative menée par la section de Kitchener-Waterloo de la YWCA (YW K-W) sur un site mis à disposition par la Ville de Kitchener. Le plan du site a été approuvé en mars 2021 ce qui a permis de procéder à une construction partielle en attendant la délivrance d’un permis de construire. L’occupation a commencé en avril 2022 pour le premier bâtiment, appelé Block Line 1 (1470, Block Line Road), qui est maintenant occupé depuis plus de 2 ans. Block Line 2, un deuxième bâtiment plus petit mais presque identique avec 10 unités familiales, a ensuite été construit au 1480, Block Line Road et a ouvert ses portes au printemps 2023. Block Line 1 a reçu le prix « Sustainable Kitchener » et le prix 2023 Branché sur le BOIS! Block Line 1 laisse espérer que cette initiative inspirera d’autres fournisseurs de logements avec services de soutien (SHP) partout au Canada. Cette étude de cas porte sur le développement initial, Block Line 1, et met en lumière les partenariats clés, les politiques gouvernementales, les considérations en matière de capital et la technologie de construction qui ont appuyé l’innovation et le succès du projet. Block Line constitue un modèle digne d’être reproduit dans d’autres régions du Canada.

English Abstract:Within one year from the date of receiving CMHC funding, 41 women experiencing homelessness within the Waterloo Region moved into their brand-new homes. These accommodations were made possible through an initiative led by the Kitchener-Waterloo chapter of the YWCA (YW K-W) on a site contributed by the City of Kitchener. The Site Plan was approved in March 2021 which allowed partial construction to proceed pending release of a building permit. Occupancy began in April 2022 for the first building, referred to as Block Line 1 (1470 Block Line Road), which has now been occupied for more than 2 years. Block Line 2, a second smaller but almost identical building with 10 family units, was subsequently constructed next door at 1480 Block Line Road and was opened in the spring of 2023. Block Line 1 is the recipient of the Sustainable Kitchener Award and the 2023 Ontario Wood WORKS! award. Block Line 1 gives hope that this initiative can serve as an example of an approach that Supportive Housing Providers (SHPs) can replicate across Canada. This Case Study pertains to the initial development, Block Line 1, highlighting the key partnerships, government policies, capital considerations, and construction technology that supported the project’s innovation and success. Block Line represents a model worthy of replication in other parts of Canada.

title: Fairness by Design: Machine Learning and Interpretable Mortgage Lending
affiliations: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology - Department of Economics and Management, University of California, Berkeley, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology - Department of Economics and Management,  and University of California, Berkeley - Real Estate Group

detail.title: Fairness by Design: Machine Learning and Interpretable Mortgage Lending
detail.abstract: Regulated lenders must explain denials and avoid disparate treatment in U.S. mortgages, yet flexible scoring can be opaque. We develop and study a less discriminatory and transparent machine-learning approach that embeds equalized-odds fairness in estimation and decomposes each decision into feature contributions suitable for adverse-action notices. Using HMDA applications, the model preserves performance while shrinking minority-nonminority error gaps and reweighting away from geographic proxies toward core underwriting signals (debt-to-income, loan-to-value). A regression-discontinuity design around underwriting cutoffs and lender-level tests confirm that the model lowers minority shortfalls at the margin and reduces withinlender disparities.

title: A Theory of Optimal Risk Layering under Budget Constraints

detail.title: A Theory of Optimal Risk Layering under Budget Constraints
detail.abstract: This paper studies the optimal allocation of a limited budget across heterogeneous disaster risk financing instruments (a reserve fund, contingent credit, and parametric insurance) to minimize expected unmet financing needs following a catastrophic event. The optimal strategy is shown to have a layered structure where instruments are ordered by marginal cost, generalizing Arrow's (1971) classical deductible theorem to three instruments with convex costs. The boundaries between layers are endogenous, determined by first-order conditions that equalize marginal costs across adjacent instruments, extending Raviv's (1979) optimal insurance design to multiple heterogeneous providers. The paper derives conditions under which an instrument is optimally excluded from the portfolio, generalizing Mossin's (1968) partial coverage result, and characterizes how the optimal composition responds to changes in budget and instrument costs.

title: A General Theory of Holdouts
affiliations: Columbia University - Columbia Business School, Students

detail.title: A General Theory of Holdouts
detail.abstract: This paper develops a principal-multi-agent framework for the holdout problem, a pervasive phenomenon in which value-creating deals fail because agents free ride on others' participation. The analysis highlights the role of the principal's commitment: Whereas a unanimity rule solves the problem under commitment, no such panacea exists under limited commitment. In that case, outcomes depend on agents' preexisting claims in a way consistent with observed patterns: senior debt used in restructurings and cash in takeovers. An increase in (partial) commitment can exacerbate the problem, generating a non-monotonicity that sheds light on contradictory findings in the literature and various policies.

title: A Dynamic Theory of Risk Layering under Endogenous Budget Constraints: Fund Capitalization, Debt Traps, and Donor Investment

detail.title: A Dynamic Theory of Risk Layering under Endogenous Budget Constraints: Fund Capitalization, Debt Traps, and Donor Investment
detail.abstract: This paper develops a theory of optimal disaster risk financing for agents whose potential losses are large relative to their fiscal capacity to self-insure. When this ratio is high (whether for a small island developing state facing tropical cyclones, a subnational government exposed to seismic risk, or any public entity whose worst-case loss exceeds its reserve accumulation capacity) the agent must assemble a multi-instrument portfolio: a reserve fund that accumulates capital over time, contingent credit that provides immediate post-disaster liquidity but generates persistent debt obligations, and parametric insurance that transfers tail risk to capital markets at a premium. The paper formulates this problem as a stochastic dynamic program with two state variables (fund balance and outstanding contingent debt) and establishes that the optimal instrument composition has a threshold structure partitioning the state space into regions with qualitatively distinct portfolios (Theorem 3), extending the static risk layering results of Cárdenas (2026a) to the intertemporal setting. A central result is the existence of a disaster trap: a region of the state space from which recovery without external assistance is impossible, generated endogenously by the interaction between debt accumulation and eligibility constraints on access to preferential credit (Theorem 4). Near the eligibility boundary, the optimal policy exhibits precautionary behavior, substituting expensive insurance for cheaper credit to preserve the option value of future access (Proposition 4). The paper characterizes the minimum initial capitalization required for the mechanism to become self-sustaining (Proposition 9) and demonstrates that fund capitalization dominates alternative external interventions (subsidizing insurance premiums or providing reactive post-disaster transfers) for sufficiently long horizons (Proposition 10). A numerical illustration calibrated to a Pacific Island State expose to tropical cyclone risk quantifies these results across three institutional regimes, showing that the statutory cap on fund accumulation is the single most consequential design parameter and that initial capitalization and institutional reform are strongly complementary. The framework applies to any budget-constrained agent facing repeated catastrophic losses; the ratio of fiscal capacity to expected losses determines endogenously whether all instruments are active and trap risk is significant, or self-insurance suffices.

title: Overconfident Forecasters and the Impact of Inflation Information: Evidence from a Randomized Survey Experiment
affiliations: Bank of Italy and UC Berkeley

detail.title: Overconfident Forecasters and the Impact of Inflation Information: Evidence from a Randomized Survey Experiment
detail.abstract: We exploit a randomized information intervention in a quarterly survey of Italian firms to study how access to recent inflation data affects deviations from the full-information rational expectations (FIRE) benchmark in managers' inflation forecasts. Treated firms receive the latest inflation reading before submitting their forecasts and, relative to non-treated firms, display less underreaction at the consensus level and less overreaction at the individual level, moving forecasts closer to the FIRE benchmark. A model that combines noisy information with overconfidence in private information provides the best overall fit to the data, outperforming alternative frameworks featuring diagnostic expectations, internal cognitive constraints, or over-extrapolation. Intuitively, with noisy information, average forecasts react sluggishly to news, so an informative public signal speeds up aggregate updating and reduces consensus underreaction. With overconfidence, managers overweight private signals and the public signal shifts weight away from private information, attenuating individual overreaction.

title: Working From Home and Wage Dynamics
affiliations: UNSW Business School and UNSW Australia Business School, School of Economics

detail.title: Working From Home and Wage Dynamics
detail.abstract: We study the relationship between working from home (WFH), wages, and wage growth using a representative sample of full-time workers. We propose a labor supply framework featuring two work modes, WFH and on-site, and develop an empirical strategy to estimate the relationships between work arrangements, wage levels, and wage growth while addressing selection into remote work. Reallocating hours toward WFH is not systematically related to contemporaneous wage levels, while higher WFH intensity predicts slower wage growth for men. An increase of eight WFH hours per week is associated with a 0.6-1.5 percentage point reduction in annual wage growth for men. For women, the corresponding estimates are generally not statistically distinguishable from zero. We show that these patterns are robust to a range of controls and are unlikely to be explained by occupational differences or selection into WFH. The findings are consistent with WFH affecting inputs into human capital accumulation and career progression, with stronger relationships for men, while having limited implications for contemporaneous productivity.

title: Formal Jobs and the Cultural Right

detail.title: Formal Jobs and the Cultural Right
detail.abstract: The rise of culturally conservative politicians has been one of the most consequential political developments of recent decades. In large emerging democracies, this trend has coincided with significant reductions in poverty, partly driven by improvements in the allocation of labor. This paper hypothesizes that the reallocation of labor toward large firms-by fostering the growth of a conservative middle class-can help explain the rise of the cultural right. To test this hypothesis, the paper leverages geocoded administrative data and differential exposure to the rise of large firms as employers in Brazil. The findings show substantial increases in support for the cultural right, driven by low-income conservatives who experience upward mobility.

title: Do Shifts in Green Energy Fund Flows Affect Financial Markets and Economic Growth?
affiliations: University of Sussex, Bank of Japan and Vlerick Business School

detail.title: Do Shifts in Green Energy Fund Flows Affect Financial Markets and Economic Growth?
detail.abstract: Why has financing related to green energy funds progressed more slowly than needed to address climate concerns, and does accelerating this transition risk undermining financial markets or economic growth? Using data on US green and brown energy funds, we examine the dynamics of capital reallocation between these two segments. We find a time-varying shift from brown to green energy investments, largely influenced by policy-driven climate news rather than long-term temperature trends. The speed of this reallocation is closely linked to changes in US climate policy. Moreover, while climate news shocks tend to depress stock returns and industrial production, these effects are significantly moderated by the presence of green energy funds, which act as a stabilizing buffer. Overall, our findings suggest that accelerated green energy fund flows can enhance both financial stability and real economic performance.

title: Fathoming Philanthropy: Transparency in Environmental Grant-making Philanthropic Foundations
affiliations: University College London - Faculty of Laws and The University of Manchester - School of Law

detail.title: Fathoming Philanthropy: Transparency in Environmental Grant-making Philanthropic Foundations

declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval through our universities

detail.abstract: Large grant-making philanthropic foundations in the UK and EU can have a significant influence over environmental law, and as such are worthy of more attention from environmental law scholars. Through analysis of publicly available documents, we identify in this paper an absence of consistent transparency by these foundations. This makes their influence hard to understand, hard to research, hard even to see at work in the world. Transparency is complex and challenging, however. And so, rather than berating problematic approaches, through interviews with actors in the field, as well as the academic literature, we explore both the difficulties that foundations experience in pursuing transparent practices and the benefits of transparency. We conclude by identifying some principles for improved visibility of foundation work.

title: Electrifying Transport in India: An analysis using Security and Emission Constrained Economy dispatch model
affiliations: Indian Institute of Management Tiruchirappalli, Indian Institute of Management Tiruchirappalli, World Bank, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Electrifying Transport in India: An analysis using Security and Emission Constrained Economy dispatch model
detail.abstract: India has set an ambitious target to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 2030. India’s electricity generation is still predominantly based on fossil fuel, although share of renewables has increasing rapidly in recent years. This paper explores the possibility of electrifying the transport sector to reduce emissions by inducting Electric Vehicles (EVs). The paper calculates the total electricity demand due to EVs for the CY 2030. It then evaluates the effect of this additional load using a security and emission constrained economic dispatch model simulated for the CY 2023. Model results show that while India’s growing EV penetration will add only a modest share to total annual electricity energy requirement, although the impact on the system peak and associated peaking generation investment and operational costs can be significant if the charging profile of the EVs are misaligned with the generation from renewables. Results also show a net increase in CO2 emissions and net decrease in Suspended Particulate Matter. Since the emissions at concentrated levels at the generating stations are economically feasible to abate, it is expected to be beneficial to the highly polluted Indian cities. There will be also an accompanying reduction of oil import bill saving foreign exchange for India.

title: Selling on Recommender Platforms: Demand Boost Versus Customer Migration
affiliations: Frankfurt School of Finance & Management,  and Frankfurt School of Finance & Management - Economics Department

detail.title: Selling on Recommender Platforms: Demand Boost Versus Customer Migration
detail.abstract: Platforms that provide product recommendations to consumers, such as marketplaces like Amazon or online travel agencies like Expedia, govern a substantial part of transactions in many markets. In addition to selling via platforms, most firms, however, also operate a direct channel. This paper investigates how the interaction between the platform channel and the firms’ direct channel affects platform design and firms' pricing incentives. We provide a rich game-theoretic model in which platforms give recommendations to consumers about products with high match value and facilitate consumer search, but charge sellers commission rates, whereas sellers compete in prices to balance demand across both channels. We show that the interaction between the channels gives rise to novel mechanisms that have counterintuitive effects. First, higher platform fees induce sellers to prioritize their direct channel—where consumers have lower expected match values and are thus more price-sensitive—leading to lower equilibrium prices. Second, improvements in recommendation quality can paradoxically reduce seller prices by intensifying the competitive pressure on the direct channel. Third, we show that for the platform, the quality of recommendations and the commission rate are strategic substitutes, that is, providing better recommendations should optimally be coupled with lower commission rates. This occurs because both instruments have potentially negative effects on seller prices. Finally, we evaluate recent policy interventions within our framework. We find that fee caps and measures that facilitate transactions on the direct channel can have unintended consequences and reduce consumer surplus by distorting the pricing incentives inherent in the dual-channel structure.

title: Bankers, Privacy and Arcana Imperii
affiliations: Luigi Vanvtelli University and Warsaw School of Economics (SGH)

detail.title: Bankers, Privacy and Arcana Imperii

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
